threads.body: [Testing] This new javaagent selector wiring is not exercised by the library-only `LogstashMarkerSelectorTest`. The analogous MDC and logger-context paths have dedicated javaagent tests and Gradle tasks covering include/exclude matching, deprecated fallback, and precedence (`javaagent/src/test/.../LogbackMdcSelectorTest.java`, `LogbackLoggerContextSelectorTest.java`, and `javaagent/build.gradle.kts:47-133`). Please add equivalent Logstash-marker javaagent coverage so property-name or resolver-wiring regressions are detected.

replies.body:
Good catch — the javaagent resolver wiring really was untested, so a wrong property name in `LogbackSingletons` would not have failed anything.

Added a `logstashMarkerTest` suite to the javaagent module with `LogbackLogstashMarkerSelectorTest`, plus `testLogstashMarkerAttributeExclusionsOnly`, `testLegacyLogstashMarkerAttributes` and `testLogstashMarkerAttributePrecedence`, all wired into `check`. It needs its own source set rather than living in `src/test` because the Logstash encoder requires logback 1.3, while the javaagent `test` source set pins 1.0.0 — same reason the library module splits it out.

Confirmed the suite observes selector behaviour rather than just passing: with `logstash-marker-attributes.included=key?` the exported record carries `key1` and `key2` and drops `other`.
